conceptual assets.information: The per-channel enable bits determine whether PWM channels operate and whether the shared clock-generator enable is asserted. The settings are also returned through configuration read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: a bus write reaches cfg_en through lines 99, 110, 183 and 184 and can change the stored enable. Availability: cfg_en disables counter operation at lines 212 and 224 and drives the clock-enable path at lines 197 and 121.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write cfg_en as zero to stop a channel's PWM activity or as one to enable an unintended channel.

conceptual assets.information: The per-channel prescaler and cycle-divider settings select the clock-generator source and divide it to determine PWM timing. PWM operation depends on this configuration and its values are available through read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: bus data writes cfg_prsc and cfg_cdiv at lines 99, 110, 183, 185 and 187. Availability: the selected clock-generator input gates counter progress at line 214, while cfg_cdiv controls tick generation at lines 215 through 219, so an unsuitable setting can withhold PWM progress.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write a prescaler or divider value that selects an unsuitable clock-generator source or makes PWM timing effectively stop.

conceptual assets.information: The per-channel polarity setting determines whether the active PWM level is represented as high or low. The setting affects the externally generated waveform and is returned through configuration read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: a bus write stores cfg_pol through lines 99, 110, 183 and 186, and cfg_pol determines the PWM level at lines 232 and 234.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could overwrite cfg_pol so an external device interprets the PWM waveform with the wrong active polarity.

conceptual assets.information: The per-channel duty setting determines the proportion of each PWM period for which the active level is asserted. PWM output behavior depends on this setting and it is returned through configuration read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: a bus write stores cfg_duty through lines 99, 110, 183 and 188, and the stored value participates in the output decision at line 231. Availability: a value such as zero can make the output remain at one level instead of providing the intended PWM activity through lines 231 to 234.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could overwrite cfg_duty with a value that produces an incorrect duty cycle or suppresses the intended PWM waveform.

conceptual assets.information: This is the per-channel address-decode decision that determines which PWM channel receives a bus access and which channel can provide the read-back value. It has no entry or exit port because it is an internal transient routing decision derived from the request address.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: the address comparison at line 109 creates the channel selection that controls the write and read routes at lines 110 and 111, so a wrong selection accesses the wrong channel. Availability: a corrupted or unmatched selection can prevent the required channel access from reaching the child at lines 110 and 111.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could cause the address decode to select the wrong channel or no channel, redirecting or losing a configuration access.

conceptual assets.information: This per-channel decision determines whether a channel's configuration is placed on its read-data output. It has no entry or exit port because it is an internal access-control decision that gates configuration read-back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: re is generated from the access fields at line 111 and controls the read-data assignment at line 194, so a changed decision can return an incorrect response. Availability: forcing re low prevents the requested configuration read from being returned through the same paths at lines 111 and 194.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the read-enable decision so a valid configuration read returns zero data or the wrong channel's data.

conceptual assets.information: The generated PWM waveform is the functional output used to control external loads or timing-sensitive devices. It is produced from the channel configuration and timing state and leaves the unit through pwm_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: the waveform is produced by the conditional assignments at lines 232 and 234 and exposed at line 117, so a compromised configuration or timing path can make the external waveform incorrect. Availability: the enable and duty decisions can hold the output at a constant level through lines 212, 224 and 231 to 234, withholding the intended PWM waveform.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt the PWM control state or output decision so the external load receives an incorrect or constant waveform.
